step_by_step_reasoning: We identify nodes visually from the whiteboard: SQS, Lambda, DynamoDB, Step Functions, Neptune, Gremlin (mapped as ThirdParty), S3, and Glue. We then map the drawn arrows to sequential flow edges: SQS triggers Lambda, Lambda interacts bidirectionally with DynamoDB to retrieve configurations, Step Functions interact bidirectionally with DynamoDB to read and write status, Step Functions trigger and scale Neptune, Gremlin executes bidirectional queries on Neptune, Gremlin exports results to S3, and S3 catalogs data to Glue.

graph.name: HomeSite Insurance Graph-Based User Relationship Pipeline
graph.notes: Serverless pipeline orchestrating ingestion of customer interactions into Amazon Neptune to build a property graph, with results exported to S3 and cataloged via Glue.

nodes.name: SQS Queue
nodes.notes: Receives events from upstream pipelines to orchestrate stages.

nodes.name: Job Initiator Lambda
nodes.notes: Triggered by SQS to retrieve configuration and initiate orchestration.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores pipeline configurations and execution exit status.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Coordinates complex, long-running ETL processes and scales Neptune.

nodes.name: Amazon Neptune
nodes.notes: Graph database hosting vertices and edges of user relationships.

nodes.name: Gremlin
nodes.notes: Traversal language and client used to query the Neptune graph.

nodes.name: Amazon S3
nodes.notes: Stores exported query results for cost-effective broad access.

nodes.name: AWS Glue
nodes.notes: Catalogs the data stored in Amazon S3.

edges.notes: Step Function writes job execution status

Neptune returns graph results to Gremlin
Gremlin exports graph query output to S3
